title: Prime Reciprocal Products: Sorry Elimination
description: Eliminates sorries and axioms from Erdős 307 formalization: proves product_rigidity (was axiom), one_helps_balance, and no_two_three_solution. Documents remaining work: p-adic disjointness and computational size bound.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #307 asks whether two finite sets of primes P, Q can satisfy (Σ 1/p)(Σ 1/q) = 1. The parent formalization has several sorry theorems and axioms. This file eliminates three of them.
overview.problemStatement: Can the sorry theorems in the Erdős 307 formalization be proved from Mathlib?
overview.text: Proves 3 of 5 sorry/axiom targets. The remaining two (p-adic disjointness, computational size bound) require infrastructure not yet available.
overview.proofStrategy: product_rigidity is a trivial iff. one_helps_balance splits the sum at 1. no_two_three_solution uses the tight bound on 3 primes.
keyInsights: product_rigidity was a trivial iff (a ⋅ b = 1 ↔ b = 1/a), not a deep result — unnecessary axiom eliminated
3 distinct primes have reciprocal sum ≤ 31/30 = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/5 (maximum over {2,3,5})
Product of bounds: (≤ 5/6)(≤ 31/30) = 31/36 < 1, ruling out the |P|=2, |Q|=3 case
Pigeonhole on primes < 5: only 2 and 3 qualify, so among 3 distinct primes at least one is ≥ 5
The remaining open cases require p-adic valuation theory (disjointness) and computational prime sum bounds (size lower bound)
The sum Σ_{p prime, p≤281} 1/p ≈ 2.009 — the computational bound needed to prove |P ∪ Q| ≥ 60

sections.title: Setup
sections.summary: Defines reciprocalSum, reciprocalProduct, and IsSetOfPrimes — the three basic predicates for the problem.
sections.mathContext: Erdős #307 asks: do finite prime sets $P, Q$ with $(\sum_{p \in P} 1/p)(\sum_{q \in Q} 1/q) = 1$ exist? The reciprocal sum $\Sigma_{1/P} = \sum_{p \in P} 1/p$ over rationals is the key object. Note: $1/2 + 1/3 + 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 + 1/13 + \cdots$ diverges, but any finite sub-sum is $< \infty$.

sections.title: Bound for 3 Primes
sections.summary: Proves reciprocal_sum_two_primes_le (≤ 5/6) and reciprocal_sum_three_primes_le (≤ 31/30). Uses pigeonhole on primes < 5.
sections.mathContext: Among 3 distinct primes, at most 2 can be in $\{2, 3\}$ (only primes $< 5$), so at least one is $\geq 5$. This gives: $\Sigma_{1/Q} \leq 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/5 = 31/30$. The `interval_cases` tactic handles the case analysis over primes $< 5$ (values 2, 3) automatically.

sections.title: No |P|=2, |Q|=3 Solution
sections.summary: Proves no prime sets with |P|=2, |Q|=3 can satisfy (Σ 1/p)(Σ 1/q) = 1. Product of bounds: (5/6)(31/30) = 31/36 < 1.
sections.mathContext: $(\Sigma_{1/P})(\Sigma_{1/Q}) \leq (5/6)(31/30) = 155/180 = 31/36 \approx 0.861 < 1$. Since the product of two positive reciprocal sums never reaches 1 in this case, no solution exists. This is proved by `mul_le_mul` followed by `norm_num`.

sections.title: 1 Helps Balance
sections.summary: Proves if 1 ∈ P and |P| > 1 then Σ 1/P > 1. Splits sum at the element 1 (contributing reciprocal 1/1 = 1).
sections.mathContext: $\Sigma_{1/P} = 1/1 + \sum_{p \in P \setminus \{1\}} 1/p = 1 + (\text{positive}) > 1$. Note: 1 is not prime, but the problem may involve $1 \in P$ in generalized form. The proof uses `Finset.add_sum_erase` to split the sum, then `Finset.sum_pos` for positivity.

sections.title: Product Rigidity (Axiom → Theorem)
sections.summary: Eliminates an unnecessary axiom: product = 1 iff sum Q = 1/sum P. This is just the algebraic fact a·b=1 ↔ b=1/a.
sections.mathContext: For $a > 0$: $a \cdot b = 1 \iff b = a^{-1}$. Since $\Sigma_{1/P} > 0$ (nonempty set of primes), `field_simp` and `mul_inv_cancel` prove this directly. The parent formalization incorrectly made this an axiom — it was never a deep mathematical fact.

sections.title: Remaining Open Goals
sections.summary: Documents the two remaining open goals: prime_sets_disjoint (requires p-adic valuation theory) and prime_set_size_lower_bound (requires computational verification of Σ_{p≤281} 1/p ≥ 2).
sections.mathContext: Two goals remain: (1) **Disjointness**: if $p_0 \in P \cap Q$, the $p_0$-adic valuation of $(\Sigma_{1/P})(\Sigma_{1/Q})$ would force a contradiction with the product equaling 1 — requires Mathlib's $p$-adic theory. (2) **Size bound**: the first 60 primes have $\sum_{p \leq 281} 1/p \approx 2.009 > 2$, requiring verified computation or Mertens estimates.

conclusion.summary: 3 of 5 sorry/axiom targets eliminated. Remaining: prime_sets_disjoint (p-adic theory) and prime_set_size_lower_bound (computation).
openQuestions: Prove prime_sets_disjoint via Mathlib's p-adic valuation
Compute Σ_{p≤281} 1/p ≥ 2 for the size bound
conclusion.implications: Sorry elimination is an important form of formalization progress. This file shows that some 'axioms' in early formalizations are actually provable theorems, and documents precisely which remaining goals require new Mathlib infrastructure (p-adic valuations, Mertens-type estimates for prime reciprocal sums).
